'''Robert J. Ulrich''' is an American [[casting director]] and [[Film producer|producer]] active since the 1980s and best known for casting television shows including ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'', ''[[The Boys (TV series)|The Boys]]'', ''[[Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist]]'', ''[[Supernatural (American TV series)|Supernatural]]'', ''[[Battlestar Galactica]]'', ''[[CSI (franchise)|CSI]]'', ''[[Diagnosis: Murder]]'' and ''[[Matlock (1986 TV series)|Matlock]]''. He has also cast most [[Ryan Murphy (producer)|Ryan Murphy]] productions since ''[[Popular (TV series)|Popular]]'' in 1999. He has been nominated for nine [[Emmy Awards]], winning a [[Primetime Emmy Award]] for casting ''Glee''. He has been nominated for the [[Casting Society of America|Artios Awards]] 22 times and won twice, for casting ''Glee'' and ''[[Nip/Tuck]]''.

==Career==
Robert J. Ulrich began his career as a stage actor, but realized he would not be successful. He moved into [[Casting (performing arts)|casting]] and says he learned more about acting his first time behind the table than in his previous career.<ref name=Roth2020>{{cite web|url=https://www.backstage.com/magazine/article/robert-ulrich-zoeys-extraordinary-playlist-audition-71217/|title=What to Know About Auditioning for Musical Series Like 'Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist'|date=July 22, 2020|last=Roth|first=Elyse|website=Backstage|others=Robert J. Ulrich (interview)|access-date=April 29, 2021|archive-date=February 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203213827/https://www.backstage.com/magazine/article/robert-ulrich-zoeys-extraordinary-playlist-audition-71217/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Wandera|first=Yvonne|date=February 10, 2015|title=Interview: Casting Director Robert Ulrich on Discovering Unknown Actors and Tips on Self-Taping Auditions|url=https://www.dailyactor.com/interview/casting-director-robert-ulrich-discovering-unknown-actors-tips-on-self-taping-auditions/|access-date=April 29, 2021|website=Daily Actor|archive-date=February 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226104327/https://www.dailyactor.com/interview/casting-director-robert-ulrich-discovering-unknown-actors-tips-on-self-taping-auditions/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Known for casting musical television series, Ulrich told ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' that "it's so much more fun when you're doing a musical, because people are singing and your day's suddenly better."<ref name=Rizzo2021>{{cite web|date=January 14, 2021|title=Casting Directors From 'Never Have I Ever,' 'Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist, 'P-Valley' and More Talk Curating Chemistry Between Co-Stars|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lists/casting-directors-behind-never-have-i-ever-zoeys-extraordinary-playlist-and-more-series-break-down-character-decisions|access-date=April 29, 2021|website=The Hollywood Reporter|last=Rizzo|first=Carita|archive-date=January 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122210552/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lists/casting-directors-behind-never-have-i-ever-zoeys-extraordinary-playlist-and-more-series-break-down-character-decisions|url-status=live}}</ref> He developed this musical casting process for the show ''Rhapsody'', which did not get [[Green-light|greenlit]]. Initially, he would have auditionees sing ''[[a cappella]]'' or with a backing track, but insisted on bringing a live pianist for the callbacks, saying in 2020 that "great singers are better with a piano and less trained singers are much better with a piano".<ref name=3Best>{{cite web|url=https://www.backstage.com/magazine/article/robert-ulrich-glee-zoeys-extraordinary-playlist-casting-director-71214/|title=The CD Behind 'Glee' Reveals the 3 Best Singers He's Ever Worked With|last=Liroff|first=Marci|author-link=Marci Liroff|date=July 24, 2020|website=Backstage|others=Robert J. Ulrich (interview)|access-date=April 29, 2021|archive-date=January 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126140742/https://www.backstage.com/magazine/article/robert-ulrich-glee-zoeys-extraordinary-playlist-casting-director-71214/|url-status=live}}</ref> He has also said that having live piano sets actors at ease.<ref name=Roth2020/> The pianist he found for the ''Rhapsody'' callbacks was [[Brad Ellis]], whom he would use for subsequent musical auditions as well as integrating into shows like ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]''. Ulrich's musical casting process has not changed since ''Rhapsody'', and he encourages actors to showcase themselves. He has also opined that for television, he considers acting ability above singing<ref name=3Best/><ref name=Out/> and that actors from the stage "should bring it down for the screen."<ref name=Roth2020/> Sometimes for auditions later in a show a pianist will not be used.<ref name=Roth2020/>

Ulrich became involved with casting for ''Glee'' through his business partner Eric Dawson, who had worked with creator [[Ryan Murphy (producer)|Ryan Murphy]] on multiple occasions; Dawson suggested Ulrich should be involved due to his musical background.<ref name=Out>{{cite web|date=March 16, 2015|title=Glee Pilot Oral History, Part 1: Casting Call|url=http://www.out.com/television/2015/3/16/glee-oral-history-part-1-can-you-imagine-glee-without-any-gay-characters|access-date=April 29, 2021|magazine=[[Out (magazine)|Out]]|last=Votta|first=Rae|archive-date=January 24, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210124190928/https://www.out.com/television/2015/3/16/glee-oral-history-part-1-can-you-imagine-glee-without-any-gay-characters|url-status=live}}</ref> While working on the show he helped develop the reality series ''[[The Glee Project]]'', which he described as an extension of the comedy-musical's casting process.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kushigemachi|first=Todd|date=March 18, 2014|title=Casting Director Robert Ulrich Keeps 'Glee' Talent Flow Open|url=https://variety.com/2014/tv/features/casting-director-robert-ulrich-keeps-glee-talent-spigot-open-1201137150/|access-date=April 29, 2021|website=Variety|archive-date=January 30, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130134431/https://variety.com/2014/tv/features/casting-director-robert-ulrich-keeps-glee-talent-spigot-open-1201137150/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2021, ''The Hollywood Reporter'' wrote that Ulrich does not find musical casting challenging, as he has many connections with triple threat performers; for ''[[Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist]]'' he cast several actors he had seen for prior auditions, including [[Jane Levy]], who had previously auditioned for him for ''[[The Rocky Horror Picture Show: Let's Do the Time Warp Again]]'', and [[Michael Thomas Grant]] and [[Alex Newell]] who had been contestants on ''The Glee Project''.<ref name=Rizzo2021/>

He is affiliated with professional guilds [[The Academy of Television Arts and Sciences]], the [[Casting Society of America]], the [[Producers Guild of America]], and Teamsters Local 399.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}}

He was also a producer of ''[[Billy Boy (2017 film)|Billy Boy]]'', a 2017 film written by and starring ''Glee'' performers [[Melissa Benoist]] and [[Blake Jenner]].<ref>{{cite AV media|title=Episode 8 - Robert J. Ulrich|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=trKkvd2jmnM|publisher=Placing Faces Podcast|via=YouTube|access-date=April 29, 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is married to actress [[Kim Johnston Ulrich]]. The couple judged the annual "Valley's Got Talent" in Ulrich's hometown of [[Modesto, California]], together.<ref>{{cite web|last=Loria|first=Keith|date=April 24, 2020|title=How The Glee Project Helped Launch These Performers to Stardom|url=http://www.playbill.com/article/how-the-glee-project-helped-launch-these-performers-to-stardom|access-date=April 29, 2021|website=Playbill|archive-date=September 28, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200928182915/https://www.playbill.com/article/how-the-glee-project-helped-launch-these-performers-to-stardom|url-status=live}}</ref>

extract: Robert J. Ulrich is an American casting director and producer active since the 1980s and best known for casting television shows including Glee, The Boys, Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist, Supernatural, Battlestar Galactica, CSI, Diagnosis: Murder and Matlock. He has also cast most Ryan Murphy productions since Popular in 1999. He has been nominated for nine Emmy Awards, winning a Primetime Emmy Award for casting Glee. He has been nominated for the Artios Awards 22 times and won twice, for casting Glee and Nip/Tuck.
